additional_info.subject: RE: ID0452780-DC/Si-D/DE-[Multi] Column Error Issue CRM:03056000040
additional_info.body:
Good afternoon Mr. Frenger,
I am reaching out from the Technical Support team in regards of ticket
ID0452780.
The ticket has been opened for outlets unavailable on chargers
MP/S8 170003980
and
MP/S8 170003981
after ELMS configuration.
I had a look at the chargers on AWS, I believe the ELMS was configured on 25.09.2025, and you experienced the outlets being OoO on 25.09.2025 and 29.09.2025 with
Errorcode:33.
Is it correct?
Starting with FW v8.0.5, a new safety approach has been introduced for what concerns chargers connected to ELMS.
The core idea is that
if ELMS is enabled and there's no active Modbus communication to provide power limits, the system defaults to a safe state by deactivating the outlets
. Therefore, you could see now all the outlets reporting OoO status with error code 33.
This is particularly crucial in scenarios like a power loss, where the ELMS might not re-establish communication immediately, preventing potential overloads. The change in 8.0.5 is a stricter enforcement of this safety principle. While it might seem less flexible initially, it aims to prevent situations where an active ELMS configuration, without live data,
could lead to uncontrolled power draw
.
Error 33 occurs specifically when
no fallback values are available
. This typically happens right after a firmware update (like to 8.0.5) if ELMS was enabled, but no power limits or fallback values have been transmitted
yet
via Modbus. The system doesn't have a known safe state to revert to.
If fallback values
have been previously transmitted
(e.g., before a reboot or power cycle), the system
will
use these configured fallback values if the ELMS connection is lost. In this scenario, the outlets should
not
be deactivated, and Error 33 should
not
appear, as the system has a defined safe operating limit.
So, the key takeaway , in case ELMS is enabled but are not actively using it, is to
ensure that a fallback value is transmitted to the device at least once.
This will allow the system to operate using that fallback in the absence of live ELMS communication, preventing the outlets from being deactivated and avoiding Error 33 during reboots or temporary communication losses.
This approach balances the need for safety with operational flexibility, ensuring that the system has a defined power limit to adhere to, even when the primary ELMS communication is absent.
I hope this clarifies your doubts. Please let me know if you need any further information.
With kind regards,

Dear Mr. Frenger,
I am following up on my previous email for ticket
ID0452780.
The ticket was opened for outlets being OoO when connected to ELMS after update to v8.0.5.
In my previous email I provided you with explanation of the new safety approach, and that in order to avoid the outlets to be OoO when connected to ELMS, a fallback value should be transmitted.
